messages:
Maya (support): OrbitPay reported a sudden p99 jump on veridian-v2 after last-night onboarding. They see p99 ~1.2s for long inputs (>16k tokens). Customer says it started ~08:30 UTC.
Eli (sre): Seen the alert. Console shows p95 up from ~240ms -> ~520ms and p99 up from ~420ms -> ~1.2s for the veridian-v2 model route. Frontend error rate small but tail latency spike correlates with long-context requests.
Cheng (ml-eng): We shipped a tokenizer variant 'bpe-xt' with veridian-v2 to improve subword coverage. Quick guess: token counts are up ~1.6x for some inputs (CJK, emoji-heavy) which increases KV cache working set and causes more KV evictions / recomputations.
Priya (oncall): Repro steps from OrbitPay: curl to /v1/generate with context length ~32k chars (they use 60k UTF-8 bytes). They provided a sample payload — sending it to repro cluster now.
Maya (support): Sample curl they sent:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"veridian-v2","input":"<redacted 32k>"}'
```
Response times: 1.15s / 1.22s / 1.17s in their logs.
Eli (sre): On repro cluster I see KV cache miss rate jump on veridian-v2 when token count > ~10k tokens, and GC-like pauses on the runtime when cache thrash happens. Also batching policy currently groups large sequences which increases scheduling latency.
Cheng (ml-eng): Two quick hypotheses: 1) tokenizer expansion -> more tokens -> more mem pressure; 2) tokenizer boundary changes produce more frequent tokenization re-chunking, preventing prefix cache hits.
Priya (oncall): Immediate mitigation options?
Eli (sre): 1) Roll back tokenizer variant for veridian-v2 to bpe-v1 (fastest). 2) Short-term routing: divert long-context traffic >16k tokens to veridian-v1 or a legacy variant. 3) Tweaks: disable coalescing for sequences >8k to avoid big batch scheduling. 4) Warm up prefix cache for high-traffic tenants.
Cheng (ml-eng): Also we can apply a tokenizer patch to keep boundary behavior but cap emitted tokens for certain classes (CJK/emojis) — but that's medium-term.
Maya (support): I'll propose two customer-facing steps: set max_context=16k client-side and we test a rollout rollback internally.
Eli (sre): Quick rollback command (internal) — run in infra deploy console:
```bash
# rollback tokenizer variant for veridian-v2
redwoodctl deploy set-variant --model veridian-v2 --tokenizer bpe-v1 --traffic 100%
```
Priya (oncall): I'm going to create a canary: pin 10% traffic to bpe-v1 and compare p95/p99 for the next 30m. If p99 drops we can increase rollout.
deploy-bot: Canary deployment started: veridian-v2 tokenizer=bpe-v1 -> 10% traffic. Check: https://console.redwood.ai/deploys/3481234567
Eli (sre): Early numbers after 10m: canary p99 down to ~480ms, baseline still ~1.15s. KV miss rate on canary lower by ~60% for same inputs.
Cheng (ml-eng): Confirms token counts on canary are ~1.0x vs 1.6x on bpe-xt. Looks like tokenizer is main culprit.
Maya (support): I'll update OrbitPay: recommend client-side cap to 16k and say we're rolling back tokenizer for everyone if canary holds. Asking for any objections.
Priya (oncall): No objections. I'll monitor for secondary effects (throughput, cost) during the rollback.
Eli (sre): Plan of record: finish canary -> if stable for 30m, promote rollback to 100% and open follow-up issue for tokenizer rework + stress test suite for long-context cases.
Maya (support): Noted. I'll send OrbitPay a temporary mitigation guide and ETA for rollback.
Cheng (ml-eng): For follow-up: add automated token-count distribution tests for onboarding jobs and add a gate that flags tokenizer variants that increase median tokenization >1.25x for any high-volume locale.
Maya (support): Thanks team. I'll close the loop with customer after rollback.
Priya (oncall): Monitoring; will post updates.
deploy-bot: Rollout to 100% completed: veridian-v2 tokenizer=bpe-v1 at 2023-11-07T09:07:12Z (job 3481234599).
